hints: Look at the array from the right end. While the numbers keep rising as you move left, can that tail be made any bigger by itself?
Find the first index i from the right with nums[i] < nums[i+1] (the 'pivot'). Swap it with the smallest number to its right that is bigger than it, then reverse the tail after i.

1. i = n−2; move left while nums[i] ≥ nums[i+1].
  2. If i ≥ 0: find j from the right with nums[j] > nums[i]; swap them.
  3. Reverse nums[i+1 .. n−1].
  4. (If no pivot was found, step 3 reverses the whole array → smallest order.)

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Generate all permutations in sorted order and find the one after the current.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Find pivot, swap with next-larger from the right, reverse the tail — all in place.

explain: For [1,3,2]: from the right, 3 ≥ 2 keeps going, then 1 < 3, so the pivot is index 0 (value 1). The smallest number to its right bigger than 1 is 2, swap → [2,3,1]. Reverse the tail [3,1] → [2,1,3]. The tail after the pivot is always in descending order, so reversing it makes it the smallest possible tail. For [4,3,2,1] there is no pivot, so we reverse everything to [1,2,3,4]. Duplicates are handled by using ≥ and > correctly.
recognize: Next larger permutation in lexicographic order, in place → find the rightmost ascent, swap, reverse the suffix.
